problems.form_value: ChatGPT (the version participants used is not stated). GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo were used only by the researchers, to score the outputs.
problems.source_says: The paper names GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo only in Section 2.3, as the models that counted uses and domains in the submissions. It never says which model ran behind the ChatGPT that participants used, so it cannot support the claim that participants did not use these models. The field's own first sentence says the participants' version is not stated. Supported wording: 'The paper names GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo only as the scoring models.' Criterion 1 is unaffected.
problems.quote: As LLMs, we used GPT4o and GPT4 Turbo, maintaining a temperature of 0 for consistency in response generation.
problems.locator: p. 5, Section 2.3, left column; whole-document search for 'GPT' (the other hits are reference titles)

problems.form_value: AI-arm participants had to use ChatGPT for the task, with no restriction on how.
problems.source_says: The paper prints one instruction for the AI arm: make sure to use ChatGPT for the task. It reports no restriction on how to use it, but it does not say that there was none, and it does not say how participants reached ChatGPT (an embedded window or their own account). 'With no restriction on how' is an inference from that silence and from the varied self-reported use on p. 6. Supported wording: 'The paper reports no instruction on how to use it.' Criterion 1 and the open_chat role are unaffected.
problems.quote: the experimental condition or ‘AI group’ (these participants were explicitly asked to make sure they used ChatGPT for the task)
problems.locator: p. 5, Section 2.2 (continued), left column; p. 6, Section 3.2.2

confirmed.statement: (a) The paper states random assignment in two places: 'After the pre-task survey, the experiment used a between-subjects design to randomly assign participants into one of two treatment conditions' and, in the Fig. 1 caption, 'Then, we used a between-subjects design to randomly assign all participants to one of the two experimental conditions (Control vs. AI).' The form's assignment quote is verbatim. randomized = yes, unit = individual and structure = between are supported.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 2.2 (continued), left column; p. 4, Fig. 1 caption

confirmed.statement: (a) No passage contradicts random assignment. The p. 4 sentence 'participants were randomly selected based on their English proficiency and prior experience with ChatGPT. This selection ensured balanced representation across both control and experimental conditions' describes how the four groups were formed, and the Fig. 1 caption places that step before assignment. The paper never says 'stratified' or 'block', as what_was_assigned says. The validation sample drew '5 from each group and condition', so both conditions occur in every group. The only other 'assign' hit, 'after assignment to subgroups' in the limitations, is about subgroup sample sizes.
confirmed.locator: p. 4, Section 2.2 and Fig. 1 caption; p. 5, Section 2.3, right column; p. 11, Section 4.3.3; whole-document search for 'random' and 'assign'

confirmed.statement: (b) What was assigned is ChatGPT use for the participant's own written piece. The AI group 'were explicitly asked to make sure they used ChatGPT for the task' and the control group 'were forbidden from using ChatGPT for the task'. In both arms the scored output is the participant's own short piece (approx. 100 words). The conditions do not differ only in whose output is evaluated.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 2.2 (continued), left column; p. 5, Section 2.3

confirmed.statement: (c) The tool is generative AI built on a language model. The paper calls ChatGPT 'a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)' that 'leverages a large pre-trained language model and can draw on it to generate novel text'. The first sentence of name_model is right: no passage names the model or tier that participants used.

(d) The comparison arm matches the form. Control participants were forbidden from using ChatGPT, Fig. 1 labels the arm 'Not using ChatGPT for writing', and the paper describes no other aid. Self-reports show 'a significant majority (90 %) in the control condition did not use any digital tools during the task'. The instruction forbade ChatGPT only, and the paper does not name the tools the other controls used. The form's control description reports the 90 percent figure, so ai = none and ai_vs_bau fit.
confirmed.locator: p. 5, Section 2.2 (continued); p. 4, Fig. 1; p. 6, Section 3.2.2

confirmed.statement: (e) Not applicable. The treatment is between subjects. Only the perception surveys repeat within person (pre and post), and the form codes no within-person contrast.

The AI arm description matches the text. Participants reported their ChatGPT use after the task: 27 percent relied entirely on ChatGPT, 47 percent made minor or major changes to the AI-generated output, 21 percent used their own prompts or a feedback loop, and 5 percent were unclassified. ai_tool.role = open_chat fits this free use of a chatbot.

The HAI dyad classes (Human-only, AI-only, AI-led, Human-AI-dyadic) come from self-reported engagement ('we categorised participants based on their engagement with ChatGPT'), not from assignment. The form keeps them out of the coded contrasts and says so in its notes.

arms[].n_randomized = null and arms[].n_analyzed = null are right. The main text prints no arm sizes. It gives only the four group counts (58, 60, 54, 53), 266 completed, 43 excluded and 225 analyzed. It does not say whether the attention check came before or after assignment.

preregistered = yes is right: 'Methods, hypotheses and analyses of the study were pre-registered online at Open Science Frame', with the link https://osf.io/dt5up?mode=&revisionId=&view_only= under Pre-registration.
design_class = online_rct fits: 'This study was conducted using the survey platform Qualtrics and participants were recruited via Prolific'.

summary: The PDF states twice that all participants were randomly assigned, between subjects, to a control condition forbidden from using ChatGPT or an AI condition told to make sure they used ChatGPT for their own written piece (p. 5; Fig. 1 caption, p. 4), so criterion 1 holds and the assignment fields, both arms and the ai_vs_bau comparison are supported. Two ai_tool phrases go beyond the text: the paper never names the model behind the participants' ChatGPT, so 'GPT-4o and GPT-4 Turbo were used only by the researchers' is unsupported, and 'with no restriction on how' states as fact a point the paper leaves unsaid.
